title: Exploring the Limits of Large Language Models as a Reflection of Human Cognition: An Illustration in the Context of Moral Judgement
abstract: arXiv:2508.06950v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, are increasingly used in research, ranging from simple writing assistance to complex data annotation tasks. Recently, some research has suggested that LLMs are able to reproduce human responses to psychological questions and may, therefore, be used as simulators of human participants in some psychological research. We caution against this approach. Based on machine learning research, we argue that LLMs are likely to behave differently on novel stimuli compared to human study participants. We exemplify this in an experiment regarding moral judgments, demonstrating that slight changes to the wording of 30 moral scenarios used in prior work significantly reduce the similarity between ratings made by humans and LLMs, although the magnitude of this reduction varies across models. translated_title: 探索大语言模型作为人类认知反映的局限性：以道德判断情境为例
translated_abstract: 诸如ChatGPT这样的大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被应用于研究工作中，从简单的写作辅助到复杂的数据标注任务。最近，一些研究表明，LLMs能够重现人类对心理学问题的回答，因此在某些心理学研究中可能被用作人类被试的模拟器。我们对这种方法提出警示。基于机器学习研究，我们认为LLMs在面对新颖刺激时的表现可能与人类研究被试不同。我们通过一项关于道德判断的实验来说明这一点：对先前研究中使用的30个道德情境的措辞进行轻微改动，就会显著降低人类评分与LLM评分之间的相似性，尽管这种降低的幅度在不同模型之间存在差异。因此，我们建议研究者针对其特定的实验情境验证人类与LLM反应之间的相似性。
tldr: 本研究警示不应将大语言模型当作人类被试的模拟器，通过道德判断实验证明对情境措辞的轻微改动即会显著降低LLM与人类评分的相似性，因此必须针对具体实验验证LLM与人类反应的一致性。
en_tdlr: This study cautions against using LLMs as simulators of human participants, demonstrating through moral judgment experiments that slight wording changes significantly reduce the similarity between human and LLM ratings, urging researchers to validate human-LLM response similarity for their specific experimental settings.
